title: Scout H-S1 (gap matrix, handover sections 2-5): accounting completeness, premium launch attribution and escalation routes, decision identity/claims/coalescing/backoff, budget reservations and quota handling
spec:
READ THE CODE AT /Users/k3ntaw/code/orchestrator/wt/goal-T-0260 (goal/T-0260 head 2ca1517), NOT your worktree base (it is stale). Read-only. Cite path:line from that tree.
Handover doc: /Users/k3ntaw/Documents/orchestrator-efficiency-handover.md sections 2, 3, 4, 5 (read those sections once).
Files to read (targeted, not whole repo): orchestrator/bus.py (normalize_usage, log_run, post_result, events), orchestrator/scorecard.py (by_goal, tokens_per_accepted_goal, accepted_goals, task_class, scores), orchestrator/planner_runs.py (decision_points, claims, _held_at, leases, reconcile, run, usage), orchestrator/goals.py (launch_planner, decision packet, budgets), orchestrator/decision.py if present, orchestrator/pool.py (budgets, cooldowns, running counters, save, codex_available, pick_executor, tally_planner), orchestrator/executor.py (start, slots, running increments, resume), orchestrator/daemon.py (tick, dispatch, free_slots, stamp, lease, complete, sweep_leases, reconcile_dead, autonomous Planner block, notify), orchestrator/handover.py (auto-handover section every 15 min), .orchestrator/pool.toml ([planner], [daemon], [limits], [review]). Tests: grep tests/ for existing coverage.
Produce a matrix, one row per handover requirement in sections 2-5, columns: requirement · status (existing and verified / partial / missing / unnecessary) · evidence path:line · gap and the smallest change that closes it (or why unnecessary) · verification (existing test name, or the test to write) · confidence 0-1.
Requirements to cover at minimum: run rows carry goal/task/run/attempt/decision ids, role, provider, model, account, client version, prompt/policy version, route reason; token buckets incremental vs cumulative, cached subset vs separate, reasoning double count; marginal spend vs API-equivalent vs quota observation kept separate; tokens per accepted goal undefined at zero accepted; median and tail per goal; premium invocations explained (count, context, output, cache, launch reasons); premium launch reason persisted with decision requested, evidence, cheaper steps tried; routine/investigate/escalate routes with deterministic rules; decision identity from goal+kind+state version; atomic claim with owner and lease; coalescing bursts into one packet; durable processed event cursor; bounded backoff on infra failures (auth, quota, unavailable) without model retries; interactive session exclusion as renewable lease vs stale file; stage stamps claim/start/complete and idempotent side effects; pinned config/prompt version per run; pre-dispatch atomic budget reservation across parallel workers with heartbeat/lease and reconciliation; quota hold produces no repair task and one notification per transition; premium headroom reserved for escalations; second account no duplicate dispatch.
Also list which of the handover's required regression cases (section Delivery order, bullet list) already have a test (name it) and which do not.
Output cap 1,500 tokens: the matrix rows first, then the regression-case list, then at most 5 lines of what surprised you. No prose introduction.
acceptance: every listed requirement has a matrix row with a status, a path:line from wt/goal-T-0260 or 'none found', and a verification entry
the regression-case list names an existing test or marks the case uncovered
output under 1,500 tokens, no code changes
